Definition: or δάκρυον of uncertain affinity; a tear:--tear.
BiblicalUsage: Tears run through the New Testament as the language of grief and of love. The woman washed Jesus' feet with her tears, Paul served the Lord with many tears under persecution, and the promise at the end is that God will wipe away all tears from our eyes. The word itself survives in the older spelling, the form the manuscripts carry where the word lists give the shorter form.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God keeps every tear, and the day is coming when He will wipe them away Himself.
RelatedTopics: Grief; Comfort; Hope; Love for God
